note: Deep-dive #8. GitHub Actions and Azure DevOps runs are real runs on the free hosted capacity. Order: green run on main, failing PR branch, attestation, Azure DevOps.
prepare: # owner signs in (device code), not recorded
Push-Location app; dotnet restore PurchaseStatus.slnx --locked-mode; dotnet test PurchaseStatus.slnx; python -m pytest security -q; Pop-Location
az group create -n rg-mglab-deep-dive-08 -l westeurope -o none
$gh = Read-Host 'Throwaway GitHub account or org name (owner types)'
az deployment group create -g rg-mglab-deep-dive-08 -f app/infra/main.bicep -p githubOwner=$gh --query properties.outputs -o json > $env:TEMP\devsecops-outputs.json
Get-Content $env:TEMP\devsecops-outputs.json | ConvertFrom-Json | Select-Object -ExpandProperty acrName   # note: put the ids into the GitHub environment (not on screen)
# manual: create a PUBLIC throwaway GitHub repo; push app/ as the repo root (git init, git add, git commit, git remote add origin, git push)

# manual: GitHub environment prod-lab (labadmin as required reviewer), environment secrets AZURE_CLIENT_ID / AZURE_TENANT_ID / AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID, variables ACR_NAME / APP_NAME / RESOURCE_GROUP; enable code scanning

# manual: Azure DevOps (organization devladlog): private throwaway project, service connection sc-mgl08-wif (workload identity federation), environment prod-lab with approval, variables acrName / appName / resourceGroup, pipeline from azure-pipelines.yml
# manual: dry run: open a PR, green, merge, approve prod-lab, confirm the app shows the image digest

screens.name: actions-run
screens.account: labadmin (GitHub account of the throwaway repo)
steps: Merge the green PR to main (or push to main) and open Actions > the secure-pipeline run on main
Show all jobs green and the prod-lab deployment waiting for the reviewer
Open the waiting job briefly to show 'Review deployments'
mask: tenant name and id, subscription id, registry host, client ids

screens.name: gate-fail
screens.account: labadmin (GitHub account of the throwaway repo)
steps: Create a PR branch with a deliberately old base image digest (or a waiver past its date) so vuln_gate.py fails
Open the failed run > the job summary: the table with finding, package and fixed version
Do not enable step debug logging

screens.name: attestation
screens.account: labadmin (GitHub account of the throwaway repo)
steps: Open the repository's Attestations page and the entry for the pushed image digest
Switch to the Security tab > Code scanning: CodeQL results
mask: registry host and digest owner details

screens.name: ado-run
steps: Open the pipeline run of azure-pipelines.yml: Build and Deploy stages
Show the environment approval prod-lab waiting, then approve it
Project settings > Service connections > sc-mgl08-wif: 'Workload identity federation' visible
mask: tenant name and id, subscription id, client ids

teardown: # manual: delete the throwaway GitHub repository and the Azure DevOps project (removes the service connection); federated credentials go with the identities
